newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen mixed to higher, peso firm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen mixed to higher, peso firm.

text.p: Traders saw Mexican stocks mixed to higher at the open on Tuesday due to upward momentum and an expected recovery on Wall Street.
"Most sectors were strong yesterday, only Telmex weighed us down because of its ADRs. If the Dow opens up, Telmex should no longer be a counterweight," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts situated resistance at 4,475 points on the IPC index, compared to Monday's close of 4,436.75.

Traders expected the peso to open stronger due to favorable market forecasts for domestic inflation data and the primary securities auction, both scheduled later in the day, and lower U.S. long bond yields.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.9350/7.9550 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9380/7.9420 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.9400/7.9430.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen easing down from Monday's close of 20.50 percent due to a firm peso and demand at what were still relatively high rates of return.
